title: Wrong Room, Right Boots
subject: a woman who walks into the wrong room at the leisure centre expecting spin class and finds a Thursday line-dancing class for pensioners, stays out of politeness, and by week three owns the boots
caption: 80s-flavoured cowgirl synth-pop, mid-2020s chart style. Gated LinnDrum kit with a driving four-on-the-floor, pulsing analog synth bass, bright stabbing synth brass, a twangy clean electric guitar playing country licks, stacked handclaps. Glossy 80s reverb, punchy wide mix. Female mezzo, sassy half-spoken verses and a big belted chorus. 122 BPM, A major. Cheeky, bright and danceable. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no dubstep drop, no banjo, no ballad slowdown.
lyrics:
[Intro - synth brass and LinnDrum]

[Verse 1]
Thursday night in cycling shorts
Room four, I thought it said
Sixteen grannies in a row
And Derek in a hat instead

[Pre-Chorus]
I should have backed out slow
But Joan already said hello

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Heel, toe, turn around
I came here to sweat
Now I'm doing the Tush Push

[Verse 2]
Week two, a western shirt
Week three, the boots were red
Joan says I kick too high
Derek nods his head

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Heel, toe, turn around
Spin class down the hall
Can keep its bikes, I'm country now

[Bridge - handclaps]
Grapevine left
Grapevine right

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Joan still runs this town
I came here to sweat
Now I'm teaching Derek how

[Outro - twangy guitar and synth bass]
Room four, Thursday night
